topic: Your 'Healthy' Breakfast Smoothie May Be Spiking Insulin More Than Whole Foods
subject: health

sources.title: Validating Healthy Eating Index, Glycemic Index, and Glycemic Load with Modern Diets for E-Health Era
Nutrient Extraction Lowers Postprandial Glucose Response of Fruit in Adults with Obesity as well as Healthy Weight Adults

facts.claim: Nutrient extraction of seeded fruits reduces the Glycemic Index compared to eating fruit whole in subjects with obesity.
facts.quote: Nutrient extraction was shown to significantly lower GI, compared to eating fruit whole, in subjects with obesity (raspberry/mango: 25.43 ± 18.20 vs. 44.85 ± 20.18, p = 0.034 and passion fruit/mango (26.30 ± 25.72 vs. 42.56 ± 20.64, p = 0.044).

facts.claim: Smoothies had a higher median number of meals (12.04) to reach an acceptable Glycemic Load of less than 20 compared to high-school (5.75) or fast-food (4.48) diets.
facts.quote: Mexican diets were the common predictor for GI and carbohydrates per meal to reach acceptable GL < 20; with smoothies (12.04), high-school (5.75), fast-food (4.48), Korean (4.30), Chinese (3.93), and liquid diets (3.71) presenting a higher median number of meals.

facts.claim: Nutrient extraction of raspberries and passionfruit mixed with mango lowers the Glycemic Index in healthy weight individuals.
facts.quote: Similar results were found in those of a healthy weight.

facts.claim: Diets with more carbohydrates and more meals were needed to reach an acceptable Glycemic Load of less than 20, including smoothies and liquid diets.
facts.quote: Diets with greater carbohydrates and more meals needed to reach acceptable GL < 20 included smoothies, convenient diets, and liquids.

research.angle: While smoothies and liquid diets require more meals to reach an acceptable Glycemic Load, nutrient extraction of specific fruits actually reduces the Glycemic Index compared to eating them whole.
research.verdict: The evidence contradicts the proposed angle by showing that nutrient extraction can lower the Glycemic Index of certain fruits, even though smoothies are associated with higher meal counts to maintain a low Glycemic Load.
research.caveat: The study on nutrient extraction specifically looked at raspberries, mango, and passion fruit rather than a general analysis of all blended fruits and vegetables.
